newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Internet law will not limit ad industry.
newsitem.headline: German Internet law will not limit ad industry.

text.p: New German Internet legislation set to take effect this week will not create new limits on the development of advertising or shopping in cyberspace, marketing experts said on Wednesday.

The new law, which comes into effect on Friday, sets new standards for child protection on the Internet and defines which activities require regulation and which can be operated without any formal licence or regulatory oversight.
But marketing industry representatives say the multimedia law does not create any new restrictions for their business on the Internet.

"The laws that have governed advertising and marketing until now of course also apply to the Internet," Hans Juergen Schaefer, legal expert for the German Direct Marketing Association (DDV) told Reuters.

He added that the new law only creates guidelines for Internet services used by individuals -- such as electronic mail, online shopping and video conferencing -- and that other limits will only come from cases addressed by the courts.
Schaeffer said even the flexibility courts have to interpret the law, called the Information and Communications Services Act, did not present new hurdles for the industry.

"I do not see an avalanche of court cases coming," Schaefer said, adding that he also did not see any "exposed flanks, where companies could wander into forbidden territory." -- Deborah Cole, Berlin newsroom, 49 30 203 98 114
